purpose: State that recursive continuation aspects are not independently fundamental outside the whole relation.
symbolic_seed: A ⇔R B is treated as an indivisible recursive process relation rather than two independently fundamental objects connected by an external operator.
plain_language_definition: Recursive continuation aspects are locally distinguishable but not independently fundamental outside the indivisible whole relation.
core_interpretation: The apparent sides and the recursive relation are aspects of one process structure rather than separable primitives.

formal_seed.aspect_form: aspect(A, WholeR) ∧ aspect(B, WholeR) ∧ aspect(⇔R, WholeR)
formal_seed.projection_rule: Analytical separation is permitted only as a restricted projection convenience.
formal_seed.ontological_rule: No separated aspect may be treated as independently complete within this phase.
formal_seed.history_rule: Residue-history belongs to the whole relation and cannot be fully isolated into a standalone component.
formal_seed.non_fragmentation_rule: Introducing separate primitive operators without necessity is treated as suspect decomposition.

allowed_uses: Treating recursive process relations as indivisible wholes.
Analyzing aspects provisionally without granting independent primitive status.
Interpreting (E≠0), δ(E>0), and ⇔R as simultaneous aspects of one closure relation.
Interpreting -1, +1, and ⇔R as aspects of recursive polarity rather than isolated poles.
forbidden_uses: Treating ⇔R as an external glue operator.
Treating process aspects as fully independent primitives.
Using analytical decomposition as ontological proof.
Introducing unnecessary secondary operators that fragment the primitive relation.
Using non-separability as proof of physical nonlocality.
Claiming QM and GR are mathematically unified.
